quotes.text: Life was good. The sun setting on a sweet summer's day, the smell of freshly mowed lawns, the sounds of children playing — A house across the river, on the Jersey-side. A beautiful wife and a baby girl. The American Dream come true. But dreams have a nasty habit of going bad when you're not looking.
First day off the sauce and, somehow, I'd still ended up in the gutter.
Collecting evidence had gotten old a few hundred bullets back. I was already so far beyond the point of no return I couldn't even remember what it had looked like when I had passed it.
God, I turned out to be such a damsel in distress.
I tried not to think about when it was that my existence became less about the things that make up people's lives and more about the holes that losing those things leave behind.
The things that I want not to be true are true, and the things that I want to be true are not true.
Life knows two miseries; getting what you don't want and not getting what you want.
A funhouse is a linear sequence of scares. Take it or leave it is the only choice given. Makes you think about free will: have our choices been made for us because of who we are?

All this time we got the fable of Sleeping Beauty wrong. The prince didn't kiss her to wake her up. No one who slept for a hundred years is likely to wake up. It was the other way round. He kisses her to wake himself up from the nightmare that has brought him there.
It was a classic mob hit. No worries. No fuss. Just another page in the obituaries.
Like so many times before, I'd found myself alone, locked on a path of destruction. It was at my worst when I was at my best.
Vladimir Lem. Dearest of all my friends. If I had known, I wouldn't have hurt you.
A fugitive undercover cop framed for murder, following a trail of blood. These people were here for the reason I'd stayed alive. One way or another, this was going to end.
I had a bullet. I had a gun. Time to go to work.
Max, we got to stop meeting like this.
I lied to myself that it was over. I was still alive, my loved ones were still dead. It wasn't over.
There are things in life you cannot choose: how you feel.
When had I ever needed to invite trouble in? It always found me, no matter where I hid.
I didn't deserve to walk away. There are no happy endings.
Nothing to do but wait. Watching the dead-end street of my life. My brain felt like a migraine waiting to happen.
Your past has a way of sneaking up on you. You'll hear broken echoes of it everywhere, like a bad replay. You'll get mad at everyone for reminding you about it, even if it's all in your head.
When you're walking in heaven, the bad things are easier to believe.
None of us was a saint.
They were all dead. The final gunshot was an exclamation mark to everything that had led to this point. I released my finger from the trigger. And then it was over.
Firing a gun is a binary choice. Either you pull the trigger or you don't.
I was still alive, and still not all that happy about it.

Einstein was right, time is relative to the observer. When you're looking down the barrel of a gun, time slows down. Your whole life flashes by, heartbreak and scars. Stay with it, and you can live a lifetime in that split second.
If there's no light, it ain't a tunnel. It's a hole.
What are you so afraid of? What do you want from me?
Another dark, rainy night. Another police station. Another futile crusade for amends. Time moves forward, and nothing changes.
The past is a gaping hole. You try to run from it, but the more you run, the deeper, more terrible it grows behind you, its edges yawning at your heels.
